title: Ways to Split Array Into Good Subarrays
summary: Given a binary array, count the number of ways to divide it into subarrays, each containing exactly one '1'.
statement: Given a binary array, count the number of ways to divide it into subarrays, each containing exactly one '1'. Return the count modulo 10^9 + 7.
constraints: Split the binary array into contiguous nonempty subarrays.
A split is good when every part contains exactly one value equal to one.
Return the number of good splits modulo 1,000,000,007.
reference_solution:
def count_good_binary_splits(nums):
    MOD=1_000_000_007;ones=[i for i,value in enumerate(nums) if value==1]
    if not ones:return 0
    answer=1
    for left,right in zip(ones,ones[1:]):answer=answer*(right-left)%MOD
    return answer

hints: Every part must correspond to exactly one occurrence of one.
Between consecutive ones, choose any one cut position.
Multiply their index distances; return zero when no one exists.
Choices between different consecutive ones are independent, and the distance equals the number of legal cut locations.
